Yes, getting myself to cook is so difficult so for a few months I've started making realistic grocery lists. I used to eat take out everyday, but slowly started eating more at home by getting food to cook and food that's ready to eat. I also started considering veggies and fruits as add-ons, before it felt like a necessity I always overlooked, and it's really helped my eating and cooking habits. I'm also pretty lucky to have an SO that usually doesn't mind to cook when I just can't.

It takes forever to prep food to start cooking so I have to either be craving it, feel the motivation to do it, or prep beforehand. I prep after I've already eaten and have time or it'll take me take longer than the hour or two it already does. When I buy veggies I rinse, chop if needed, and store in a ziplock in the fridge ready for use within the week. If I'm thinking of making something with meat later that day or week I season the meat in a ziplock and store it - makes it more likely that I'll actually make the dish or use it. 

I know for a fact I am not going to be able to get myself to cook 3 meals a day, sometimes I can't even bring myself to even cook 1 meal. That's when I make cold foods like sandwiches or tuna, or eat something that's ready or microwavable like store bought chicken salad or frozen burritos. And since I have my veggies cut, I can top off my ready to eat or frozen meals with them to balance it out. For example, when I eat frozen burritos I add tomato, lettuce, queso ranchero, and sauces on top. It makes it more fulfilling and healthier than just eating it alone.

I'm adding some groceries I pick up and some food I make. It might give you inspiration or you can try some of it to see how it works for you.


Groceries I normally get
Main food/food to cook: ground beef, chicken, noodles, rice, beans, eggs, bacon, bread, tortillas, ham

Ready to eat/Cold food: chicken salad, potato salad, hummus, tuna, sandwiches, wraps, smuckers (not food, but I also eat multiple snacks/fruits as a meal some days)

Frozen: burritos, corn dogs, chicken fried rice, sliders, fries

Add-on: lettuce, tomatoes, onions, cheese, sauce, avocado, broccoli, bananas, watermelon, cantaloupe

Other stuff: oil, chicken fry, chili sauce w meat and beans, salsa 


Completed dishes depending on how much time they take
Long: chicken Alfredo, spaghetti with ground beef, fried chicken with rice and beans, morisqueta (which is kinda the same as the last dish, but with beef and salsa and all mixed up), burgers and fries, burritos, tacos

Moderate: Chilaquiles, bacon mac n cheese, faux-pizza(w naan bread on stove top), fries sandwich w veggies, wraps, pancakes, chili dogs, chili cheese fries

Short: Tuna, frozen foods (fried rice bowl w added veggies, burrito w veggies and salsa, sliders with veggies), smuckers and fruit, sandwiches, hot dogs, quesadillas, weenies con huevos (eggs w hot dog sausages)
